The picture is silent: audio: { clip: <the same address>, spatial: true } on the object plays its sound from the screen - pbr: true derives Patina normal, roughness, and metalness maps from a raster texture - repeat: [u, v]; copies of the picture across the surface (the default fit); under wrap: "repeat" a multiplier on the tiling's density: textures tile at one repeat per world meter on every face of every primitive; 2 = twice as dense. textureScale (meters per tile) is the same dial's older spelling. - wrap: omitted, the picture fits once across the surface, on the shape's own 0..1 UVs: an equirectangular map wraps once around a sphere, a poster fills a plane once, a label runs once around a cylinder's side; repeat then counts copies. "repeat" is the one word that tiles it (the tiling above: fabric, brick, felt); the texture's name never decides. A scripted body samples its own UVs and tiles them unless "clamp" - metalness/roughness: PBR material properties (0-1) - emissive: Glow color (glows at strength 1 on its own), emissiveIntensity: glow strength - unlit: true skips lighting; the color/texture and emissive land flat, no shade or shadow on the surface (default false) - opacity: 0..1, blends in linear light: over a dark background one white layer at 0.07 reads 28% solid, 0.015 reads 7%; a primitive with no side draws both faces, so 0.07 reads 44%, 0.015 13% - view: a place's live picture on the surface: a door's glass onto another place, or this place from a camera (see `view` field doc) - canvas: the live picture of a <canvas> the game's ui draws into, by its id (see `canvas` field doc) | { kind: "water"; how much of the floor the water hides (default: 0.3; 1 is a solid sheet) - waveIntensity: 0-1 (default: 0.15) | { kind: "scripted"; color?: Color; emissive?: Color; emissiveIntensity?: number; metalness?: number; size?: number } | null } // Scripted material; a script you write builds the material at render time - script: path in scripts/ exporting `material(ctx)` that returns a node material (import from "builtin/tsl" for TSL nodes, from "builtin/three" for node material classes) - params: values passed to the script; numbers, booleans and lists are live uniforms via ctx.param(name, default): a change patches with no recompile, save a list's new length or row width and a value the script reads in plain JS. A list of numbers, or of rows of 2 to 4 numbers, is a table that ctx.param(name, list).element(i) reads by row - the standard fields below land on the material the script builds; a node slot the script authors (colorNode, emissiveNode, …) shadows the field under it. The texture fields are the script's: it samples its own with ctx.texture(cdn), and the ui's <canvas id> with ctx.texture("canvas://<id>"). - a positionNode that reads `time` redraws the object's shadow every frame: `m.castShadowPositionNode = positionLocal` casts the shape at rest The whole material(ctx) contract, the ctx inputs, the surface laws, the failure contract: `spawn api builtin/three` (the material and its ctx) · `spawn api builtin/tsl` (the nodes). // the member with no kind is StandardMaterialSpec: `spawn api StandardMaterialSpec` prints its notes // MaterialSpec, kind "water" underwater?: UnderwaterSpec // The bounded underwater view; present by default. enabled:false disables it. waveFrequency?: number // Unitless spatial scale; default 7.3728 for this water material. Higher values make shorter waves; lower values make longer waves. Each wave stays at full strength up to half the sheet's smaller X/Z span, fades from half to one span, and is absent beyond that span. waveHeightScale?: number // Wave height multiplier; 0 makes a flat sheet. flowDirection?: [number, number] // Flow direction in world X/Z on a level sheet. It is normalized. On a face steeper than 60° (a fall, a standing capsule's side) the water runs down the face under gravity whatever this says. flowSpeed?: number // Flow speed control; 0.1 moves foam about 1.2 metres per second. roughness?: number // Surface roughness, 0 to 1. normalScale?: number // Ripple detail scale; larger values make smaller ripples. detailNormalStrength?: number // Ripple normal strength; 0 removes small ripples. foamColor?: Color // Foam color, lit by the scene. foamStrength?: number // Overall foam strength; 0 removes foam on a level sheet. A fall (a face steeper than 60°) is aerated by its flow whatever this says: flowSpeed 0 is a still glass sheet. foamScale?: number // Foam pattern scale; larger values make smaller patches. contactFoamWidth?: number // Contact band width in metres. shorelineFoamStrength?: number // Foam strength at shores and objects. shorelineFoamSoftness?: number // Softness of the shoreline foam edge. crestFoamCoverage?: number // Fraction of wave crests that can foam, 0 to 1. crestFoamStrength?: number // Foam strength on wave crests. causticsEnabled?: boolean // Enable moving light patterns on submerged objects. causticStrength?: number // Strength of the submerged light patterns. causticScale?: number // Scale of the submerged light patterns. depthColorDistance?: number // Distance in metres over which water takes its deep color. refractionStrength?: number // Strength of the surface view distortion; 0 disables it. swellAmplitude?: number // Height of long sea swells in metres; 0 disables them. swellDirection?: [number, number] // Long swell direction in world X/Z. It is normalized. surfWidth?: number // Width of the breaking surf zone in metres. wakeSeconds?: number // How long, in seconds, the wake a body leaves on this water stays in the picture: the drawn rings and foam fade, and are gone this long after the last body nearby stops moving. Unset: the wake this water draws by default. // MaterialSpec, kind "scripted" emissive?: Color // emissiveIntensity scales it alphaTest?: number // three's alphaTest: the alpha cutoff (0..1) under which a texel is cut renderOrder?: number // draw order among transparent things (higher draws later) underwater?: UnderwaterSpec // Underwater view within this surface's own geometry. Omit for an ordinary material. drawsOver?: string[] | { parts: string[]; strength?: number; angle?: number } // a model part: the same word as a standard part's `drawsOver`: the parts of its own character this scripted part shows through when they cover it; the script keeps its shading outline?: boolean | { color?: Color; width?: number; warm?: number; lightness?: number } | null // an ink line around it: true = a 2-pixel line in a darker shade of its own colour, lit as it is lit; width = that many pixels (of a 1080p picture) up close, up to 63 pixels of the picture drawn; color = shown as given, up to 0.9 of white on each channel; with no color, lightness = the shade's share of its surface's lightness (0..1, default 0.58) and warm = how far the shade leans to a warm brown (0..1, default 0); every line thins with distance and fogs as the world does; drawn only around opaque solids view?: { link: string; oneWay?: boolean; spill?: number; sound?: number } | { camera: ViewCamera; cadence?: string; size?: number } | null // A portal glass: the surface is an aperture onto the linked world (the same `view` a standard material takes: `oneWay`, `spill`, `sound` included) and the script reads it with `ctx.view()` / `ctx.portal`: the portals skill's glass (→portals). `view: { camera }` shows this place from a camera, and `cadence` and `size` set its pictures' rate and pixels, as on a standard material.

// MaterialSpec, kind "water"
  underwater?: UnderwaterSpec   // The bounded underwater view; present by default. enabled:false disables it.
  waveFrequency?: number   // Unitless spatial scale; default 7.3728 for this water material. Higher values make shorter waves; lower values make longer waves. Each wave stays at full strength up to half the sheet's smaller X/Z span, fades from half to one span, and is absent beyond that span.
  waveHeightScale?: number   // Wave height multiplier; 0 makes a flat sheet.
  flowDirection?: [number, number]   // Flow direction in world X/Z on a level sheet. It is normalized. On a face steeper than 60° (a fall, a standing capsule's side) the water runs down the face under gravity whatever this says.
  flowSpeed?: number   // Flow speed control; 0.1 moves foam about 1.2 metres per second.
  roughness?: number   // Surface roughness, 0 to 1.
  normalScale?: number   // Ripple detail scale; larger values make smaller ripples.
  detailNormalStrength?: number   // Ripple normal strength; 0 removes small ripples.
  foamColor?: Color   // Foam color, lit by the scene.
  foamStrength?: number   // Overall foam strength; 0 removes foam on a level sheet. A fall (a face steeper than 60°) is aerated by its flow whatever this says: flowSpeed 0 is a still glass sheet.
  foamScale?: number   // Foam pattern scale; larger values make smaller patches.
  contactFoamWidth?: number   // Contact band width in metres.
  shorelineFoamStrength?: number   // Foam strength at shores and objects.
  shorelineFoamSoftness?: number   // Softness of the shoreline foam edge.
  crestFoamCoverage?: number   // Fraction of wave crests that can foam, 0 to 1.
  crestFoamStrength?: number   // Foam strength on wave crests.
  causticsEnabled?: boolean   // Enable moving light patterns on submerged objects.
  causticStrength?: number   // Strength of the submerged light patterns.
  causticScale?: number   // Scale of the submerged light patterns.
  depthColorDistance?: number   // Distance in metres over which water takes its deep color.
  refractionStrength?: number   // Strength of the surface view distortion; 0 disables it.
  swellAmplitude?: number   // Height of long sea swells in metres; 0 disables them.
  swellDirection?: [number, number]   // Long swell direction in world X/Z. It is normalized.
  surfWidth?: number   // Width of the breaking surf zone in metres.
  wakeSeconds?: number   // How long, in seconds, the wake a body leaves on this water stays in the picture: the drawn rings and foam fade, and are gone this long after the last body nearby stops moving. Unset: the wake this water draws by default.

// MaterialSpec, kind "scripted"
  emissive?: Color   // emissiveIntensity scales it
  alphaTest?: number   // three's alphaTest: the alpha cutoff (0..1) under which a texel is cut
  renderOrder?: number   // draw order among transparent things (higher draws later)
  underwater?: UnderwaterSpec   // Underwater view within this surface's own geometry. Omit for an ordinary material.
  drawsOver?: string[] | { parts: string[]; strength?: number; angle?: number }   // a model part: the same word as a standard part's `drawsOver`: the parts of its own character this scripted part shows through when they cover it; the script keeps its shading
  outline?: boolean | { color?: Color; width?: number; warm?: number; lightness?: number } | null   // an ink line around it: true = a 2-pixel line in a darker shade of its own colour, lit as it is lit; width = that many pixels (of a 1080p picture) up close, up to 63 pixels of the picture drawn; color = shown as given, up to 0.9 of white on each channel; with no color, lightness = the shade's share of its surface's lightness (0..1, default 0.58) and warm = how far the shade leans to a warm brown (0..1, default 0); every line thins with distance and fogs as the world does; drawn only around opaque solids
  view?: { link: string; oneWay?: boolean; spill?: number; sound?: number } | { camera: ViewCamera; cadence?: string; size?: number } | null   // A portal glass: the surface is an aperture onto the linked world (the same `view` a standard material takes: `oneWay`, `spill`, `sound` included) and the script reads it with `ctx.view()` / `ctx.portal`: the portals skill's glass (→portals). `view: { camera }` shows this place from a camera, and `cadence` and `size` set its pictures' rate and pixels, as on a standard material.
